title: Graphing a Left-Shifted Two-Thirds Power Function
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Analyze and describe the graph of y = (x + 1)^(2/3) by identifying its parent function, transformation, cusp location, domain, range, and intercepts.

steps.title: Identify the Parent Function and Horizontal Shift
steps.explanation: The parent function is y = x^(2/3) = (cbrt(x))^2, which is defined for all real x and has a sharp cusp at the origin (0, 0). Replacing x with x + 1 shifts the graph 1 unit to the left.
steps.why: Real cube roots exist for all real numbers, and squaring ensures non-negative outputs.

steps.title: Determine the Cusp, Symmetry, Domain, and Range
steps.explanation: The cusp moves from (0, 0) to (-1, 0), and the graph is symmetric about the vertical line x = -1 with range [0, infinity).
steps.why: Since (( -1 + u ) + 1)^(2/3) = u^(2/3) = ((-u) + 1 - 1)^(2/3), the curve is symmetric about x = -1.

steps.title: Locate Intercepts and Guide Points
steps.explanation: The graph touches the x-axis at its cusp (-1, 0), crosses the y-axis at (0, 1), and passes symmetrically through (-2, 1), (-9, 4), and (7, 4).
steps.why: Choosing x + 1 = +/-1 and +/-8 makes the cube root an integer (+/-1 and +/-2).
